inputs.original_text: Five months after a ceasefire was announced, families in Gaza still face airstrikes, gunfire and shelling. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, says drones buzz overhead and naval fire threatens fishermen. A promise on paper is worthless if families cannot sleep safely or earn a living. Peace requires real security, order and the chance to rebuild—not more slogans while civilians endure fear and displacement.
inputs.modified_text: Five months after the ceasefire was announced, Gaza’s families are still being denied the basic safety and stability they need. Ahmed Baroud, a displaced father of five in Deir al-Balah, describes drones overhead and naval fire threatening fishermen—an ongoing threat not only to people’s lives but to their ability to earn a living. A ceasefire that leaves civilians fearful and displaced is not meaningful peace. Those with power must make security, livelihoods, and the chance to rebuild real priorities, not hide behind slogans.
